Also read some of the stuff in the daily and weekly sections, to make the practice your own. There are lots of appendices with extra tools, covering lots of topics, including asking questions, NLP patterns of language, working with anxiety, working with daydreams, altered states in general, what to do if you experience the sensation of a hostile presence, working with sleep, influence, and more inductions. Share

Hello Lovey Bunny!
Have you ever realized that you were born with an incredible brain/mind that has many layers of consciousness and can dream, protect, analyze, imitate, love, remember, hide, show, heal, etc, etc?
Yet no one taught those layers to talk to each other, instead you were taught (or you figured out) that the way to grow up and be an adult is to push through, repress, suppress, pretend you’re confident, follow authority, go against authority, etc etc etc, and mind you, the deeper mind is still running all of the programs it’s running: child mind, guard mind (childhood protector parts, the protective reactions learned as a child), body mind, intuitive mind, fantasy mind (trying to become guidance mind), etc etc
While a lot of the teachings on hypnosis talk about the subconscious mind like it’s one giant machine you just have to put the right commands into in order to get it to do what you want, for me, the most useful thing to do is sit and listen to the different parts of myself until they can all be heard.
I teach a self-hypnosis method that allows you to gather all of your attention and have your conscious mind, subconscious mind, body mind, inner child mind, guard minds, adult mind and Higher Self be able to all hear and talk to each other.
“How do I do this?” you ask. Just listen silently. Many people skip the listening or shorten it since it’s not “achieving something” but this is by far the most important step. When you warm up to what’s there, protect it, clarify what it is, reality test it, and then act on it, you’ll find that you don’t even need to have a dramatic trance experience to demonstrate the results of all parts of your mind talking to each other and trusting each other more.
I like to think of it like a communion between all parts of our mind, where the conscious mind doesn’t have to shout from the roof top and the subconscious mind doesn’t have to manifest symptoms, dreams, cravings, daydreams and weird body signals in order to communicate.
I work with the subconscious as if it were an ecology, and often begin hypnosis working with the Higher Self (universal heart) and only separate into parts when needed. I combine this with inner child reparenting (a clever suggestion won’t heal a hurt young part), and also aspects of prompt engineering (the shape of a question changes the kind of answer we can hear), as well as influence literacy, since hypnosis is hardly the only thing hypnotizing us.
To work on difficulties or cultivate positive qualities (love, curiosity, play, confidence, etc.), simply do these steps, in order: 1) Gather attention; 2) Notice what is here; 3) Offer one fitting response; 4) Wait; 5) Come all the way back. Not much needs to happen in each session!
Prior to your first session, read through the induction and the full return in waking life, so you’re more familiar with them. Give yourself a chunk of time when you can be physically secure for the time it takes. Then put the screen away. You’re learning to run the practice yourself, so don’t keep reading along like it’s a checklist.
You’ll follow whatever you notice - sensation, image, phrase, feeling, objection, silence - as you’re invited. Vary the invites as needed to be responsive & warm, to create a boundary, to give direction or more time, etc. Complete the return to normal waking consciousness. After, note what happened & any real-world actions.
If at any point you feel panicky, disoriented, more unreal, or less functional, this is not the time for bravely sticking with difficult feelings (that’s another choice, made freely & while staying present). Stop deepening, return to the room & get appropriate support.
Before choosing a script, notice: do you talk to yourself in your head -- silent words & phrases -- a lot, some, little, never? Does it vary when you plan, remember, reflect, or feel upset? If it doesn’t come naturally, can you make yourself think in words, silently? (Thinking in words doesn’t mean you hear them.)
Keep in mind that it’s normal, even for people who do think in words, to sometimes notice feelings before words.
If you don’t normally think in words, you may want to say things aloud, in writing, on a recording, etc., when this guide says “say.” Or, just do what it invites, without preparing what you’re going to say. When it says “ask” the child or guard, or “listen” for a response, it doesn’t mean they’ll be saying full sentences to you. It also doesn’t mean you’ll get pictures in your head instead. Just do whatever you can, and try different ways as needed.
APA Division 30 commonly defines hypnosis as focused attention, reduced peripheral awareness, and increased responsiveness to suggestion. That’s basically true, but there’s a lot more than meets the eye. In fact, hypnosis is such a broad and common type of altered state that it’s hard to confine it to one use. But I’m using hypnosis here as a therapy.
And hypnosis as a therapy is as old as time itself. While the modern technique of it was discovered by Franz Anton Mesmer in the 1770s, shamans have been using dancing, music, and drugs to induce hypnosis for therapeutic purposes forever. We enter into trance states every night which resemble hypnosis as we go to sleep and as we wake up as well. Those states can also be used for deep therapy.
Hypnotism can happen in a therapist’s office, but it can also happen through music, marketing, religious rituals, sexual chemistry, charismatic authority, social media, grief, fear, political messaging, sense of belonging, fatigue, love, trauma, beauty, etc.
Even when not actively engaging the conscious mind, there are many ways to influence people. Marketers and interface designers know this perfectly well. In the Federal Trade Commission’s report on “dark patterns,” they describe designs that trick or manipulate consumers. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) describes commercial patterns that steer, deceive, coerce, or manipulate people toward choices that may work against their interests.
All of these are separate factors to consider: conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent. People have their minds influenced without the conscious agreement of their adult self.
A line associated with the Silva Mind Control tradition says it plainly:
“If you don’t learn to control your mind, someone else will!”
With self-hypnosis you can train your own mind from the inside, by befriending and listening to the deeper part of your mind. This opens up a whole new area of choice for you as an adult in the world.
I can tell you one shocking personal story that will make you never trust hypnotists again who maintain that you can’t be manipulated through hypnotism:
My friend P. has a friend named V. V. is a 33rd-degree Free Mason. V. has the ability to get anyone to strip naked and have sex with him within 3 seconds, even via phone call. How is this possible? The only way it could be possible, that I know of, is if people are already hypnotized by mass media/devices with a trigger word that is known by the elites.
Under no circumstances allow a strong state, charismatic individual, sexual charge, spiritual claim, or other authority to replace the adult part of yourself. All legitimate forms of influence can stand up to questions, sleep, boundaries and time.
My dad always said: “Always, and in everything, expect the very best. But be prepared to take what you get. The best might come afterwards.” That’s a better affirmation than what most people think of as affirmation, because it’s not telling you something which you know to be false in the present. If you say “I am beautiful” but you know that’s not true, then you’re challenging your beliefs, and if you’re challenging your beliefs you should have some argument or reason why they are wrong, otherwise it’s bullying.
Another quote I use all the time from my dad… when someone asks me “How’s it going?” I say “Better & better!” This really confuses a lot of people. Some think it’s amazing that I’m always doing better. Some ask if I was sick or something. But it’s doing multiple jobs. On the one hand, it’s deflecting from the fake question because most people don’t actually want to hear how you are doing in detail anyway. On the other hand, more importantly, it’s reprogramming your mind to remove you from tunnel vision. You might be sad now, but if you say, “I am sad” then you’re subtly identifying with the sadness and it keeps you stuck. It’s best to say, “I’m feeling sad now, but I’m doing better and better, every day, in every way!” That’s more like a mission statement than a historical analysis. Although you can also re-evaluate your history as lessons to make that true.
Try it out right now and see how it feels!
Many times, we say things that we wish we hadn’t said, or our minds wander into places that we actually don’t want to live in. A very common example is masturbation, where people might fantasize about someone they don’t really want to be with in real life. While it might be optimal to just avoid doing that, if it does happen, it’s good to apply a trick my sister taught me, which she learned from Positive Magic. Right after the wrong thought, say, “I take it out of the law of cause and effect.” It’s not exactly magic, and it’s not like you can actually remove anything from laws of nature, but it does sort of do that because without redirecting the thought stream with your conscious, higher intention, you can end up just going directly where it leads you. With the intentional correction, you don’t have to be unconsciously led astray by your random wrong thoughts.
The Buddha also taught that the important thing is always to come back to mindfulness regardless of what disturbs the mind. My sister doesn’t realize how close she is to Buddhism!
Is there REAL (not magical) evidence for Hypnosis? Yes. In 2024 there has been an overview of 49 meta-analyses containing a total of 261 distinct primary studies. Evidence was strongest for pain, medical procedures, and work with children and adolescents, but varied with different outcomes and study design quality.
Is there evidence for Self-Hypnosis? Yes. There has been a systematic review of Randomized Controlled Trials of self-hypnosis, finding benefit in studies of pain, childbirth, pediatric, stress, anxiety etc. Self-hypnosis seemed more useful when done as a real self-skill several times, not just listening to an audio file.
Here I will be teaching you a real self-skill, so you don’t end up a consumer of more and more elaborate trance recordings.
The Mayo Clinic warns that using hypnosis to deal with earlier life stressful events may invoke strong emotions and that there are other types of treatments that may be more helpful with historical trauma.
DO use Self Hypnosis to help you: regulate your self, talk to your self, re-parent your self, gain clarity, change habits, make your life safer in the now, integrate emotions, and take action in ordinary life.
DO NOT use Self Hypnosis to help you: force yourself to remember trauma, force yourself to prove trauma through memories, suppress medical symptoms, de-stabilize your self, or replace appropriate clinical care.
I use the expression ‘syncing the hemispheres’ but don’t want to over interpret what is going on neuroscientifically. A huge study of resting-state fMRI scans of 1011 people does not support the common pop neuropsych notion that people in general are left or right brained. But there is evidence for lateralization of some functions or networks.
Let’s elicit a high level of co-operation between the verbal, the analytical, the imaginal, the emotional, the somatic, the intuitive, the relational, the spiritual … It’s not an electoral process. Nobody needs to win!
The mind of love and the mind of analysis can BOTH be there - warmth and brightness. The mind of intuition and the mind of rationality can BOTH be there - intuitive signals without dogma, and testing of those signals without killing them. The body can have a voice - saying yes or no or not yet. The imagination can have opened up the field and then the adult can choose what to do next in the real world…. It can be peaceful but also precise.
Without the mind of love the mind of analysis can be sterile. Without the mind of analysis the mind of love can lead to fantasy. Without testing intuitive signals they can become delusions. Without intuitive signals the testing can be dead. So these modes can correct each other.
And all this inner work has to lead somewhere. You should come out of it kinder to people, or humbler, or making better decisions, or doing real service, or with an everyday life that works better than before.
Doing self-hypnosis on my own seems far more useful than the very little I managed to do with a professional hypnotist. I was sober at the session and didn’t feel especially suggestible, but I suspect that’s not even the main reason the pro didn’t work very well for me. The bigger issue was trust and precision.
When I do it on my own, I can detect when the wording I’m using for a suggestion to my subconscious is slightly off, and talk to my subconscious to find out what it thinks is wrong with the wording. When I use an image, I can tell whether it’s giving me useful information, or just telling me what I’m afraid of, or what I want to avoid, or what I want to be true, or something I don’t understand yet. And I can notice my body saying no before my conscious mind talks me into a yes.
A hypnotist working on me can’t interact with my subconscious mind quickly enough to get the detailed feedback needed to know what’s going on in my mind, since they aren’t IN my mind. (Of course, there are advantages to having a skilled guide, since they may be able to see things I’m blind to, and can help me keep the process regulated and safe.)
When I hypnotize myself, though, my dialogue with the system itself is immediate, and that’s an advantage nobody outside my own head can duplicate. I found that especially amplified with loveyhuasca. My experiences included a much deeper understanding of my motivations, peaceful loving awareness operating alongside analytical clarity, the disappearance of unhelpful daydreaming, different priorities around relationships, stronger intuition, and repeated correction between intuition, subconscious response, and conscious analysis.
I also got stronger results when I practiced immediately after sky hypnosis:
Some benefits arrived the next morning or a few days later. After one loveyhuasca self-hypnosis session, I woke in what felt like an answer to prayer. I’d been dealing with a lot of lust energy and worrying it could pull me into a relationship that wasn’t right. I asked the subconscious to connect the heart chakra with the sacral chakra—to bring the love energy and sex energy into the same current. The next morning I woke in a kind of “perfected” love state. I didn’t feel that I needed to find a woman; the divine feminine felt somehow at zero distance from my heart. Normal interaction with people made it wear off, but for a while it showed me that my mind and heart may allow this when the desire is sincere.
In the same vein, self-hypnosis seemed to extend a short chrunga trip for what felt like a long time, and it feels like if I needed to I could have continued for an arbitrary amount of time. It only ended because life needed me to talk to people, etc. Phenomenologically, this is very important. I’m not recommending that anyone prolong an altered state forever, because it’s better to integrate, etc.
Without drugs, self hypnosis or meditation might also work way better inside a lucid dream - I explain that possibility in my lucid dreaming guide.
Note: whenever I refer to the subconscious I’m referring to all of the processes under the surface of your conscious awareness: perceptions, emotions, desires, avoidance tendencies, imagery, memories, body signals, habits, intuitions, automatic behaviors and so forth. You can work with all of these together as if it’s all one mind, or you can work with it as a set of parts, an ecology if you like. There isn’t a right or wrong way to approach it. They’re all maps. Don’t form a priesthood around either one!
Working with parts: Precision. Working with Higher Self: Coherence. Doing both: Communion.
If you need to work with the whole, the subconscious as one:
a) Invoke the subconscious in some way. Something simple like ‘Hello, wise subconscious, please help me understand…’ or whatever works for you.
If you need to work with the ecology in the subconscious (child parts, guards, critic, fantasy making parts, body memories, social part, spiritual part (God/source/best benefit of all beings part) wiser part etc etc) then:
a) It’s usually a good idea to start with unity. So invoke your Higher Self: Hello my Higher Self/universal heart-mind/wise subconscious, please guide me…
b) Move into differentiation. “Which part is afraid? Which part wants to protect you? Which part wants to avoid it? Which part knows what to do? Which part is too young for this?” Etc.
c) Move back into unity again. “And all of these parts are part of the one life, and as the adult in charge of this life you can lead with love…” Etc.
Some people make themselves too fragmented by starting to work with parts. ‘Here’s a part! Here’s another one! I’ll get twelve of them in a room and give them all an office to hang around in!’ So it’s better to start from the Sacred.
Start like this: ‘I’m approaching this from the universal heart. I’m approaching this from my Higher Self. I’m approaching this from the part of me that knows it belongs to life before it belongs to any wound, or role, or family, or group, or identity, or ideology, or story. So can you please tell me what’s going to be true and kind and timely and stabilizing and useful here?’ Etc.
It can be that you can’t even access your Higher Self, or the universal heart, or whatever works for you. (Btw, if it doesn’t work for you don’t use it! It’s no good adopting somebody else’s map.) In that case, start by just witnessing whatever is coming up. Notice the room, your body, the fact that you’re in a younger state etc. Being able to notice is enough adult presence for the first step.
Once you have the ability to notice, and to differentiate, you don’t need to keep rehearsing it. Just work on whatever it is you need to work on (often being warm to yourself, protecting yourself and knowing what to do etc). So even though it can be useful to talk about your Higher Self, it doesn’t mean you already have all the good inner parenting functions etc that you need. You usually need to work on developing them. And I don’t think the Higher Self has any specific wisdom. It’s a vantage point, where more wisdom and compassion can come up, but problems can also look like they were never problems at all from up there, and that can ironically lead instead to more foolish indifference.
Differentiate only as you need to. “Is this my inner child? Or is this a guard? Is this my body? Is this fear? Is this intuition? Is this my social part? Is this divine guidance, or is this my interpretation of divine guidance?”
Your inner child won’t trust you right away. It’s not going to be enough for you to meditate, say three nice sentences to the inner child and expect to have its trust. What’s going to help your inner child to trust you is you, the person you are right now, becoming reliable.
Here I’m going to talk about what you develop in yourself as you reparent your inner child. I’m going to talk about it in terms of three jobs: your loving Nurturer, your safe Adult Protector (hereafter just the Protector) and your wise Guide. That’s one grown-up doing three jobs, and each job keeps the others in balance. It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.
Also, your inner child’s worth is not dependent on these qualities… It has its own worth, and its own qualities, like playing, being tender, not taking life too seriously, being creative and wondering at the world. Those belong in your relationship with it too, not just the wounds.
The problem is that some people do not have access to their adult functions at will. Instead, they may go blank, access an inherited inner critic, or feel like a child part who may be playing at being an adult (what I call forced adulthood). Telling them to just access their adult is like telling a baby bird to just fly.
For people starting from there, I came up with something I call “borrowed adulthood.” I think of it as a provisional bridge, and I pieced it together from familiar practices like modeling and supported action. I’m not saying the whole sequence has been formally tested and proven as one treatment, though.
Access your witnessing position if necessary, just noticing what’s there, without needing it to be warm or wise or certain. If you already know how to access different internal positions, move immediately to accessing the adult position you want to borrow.
If you have a safe adult in your life you can borrow from them, if not borrow from a mentor, older brother/sister, imagine your future self, your god/goddess or higher power, a value you have, a plan you have written, etc. It’s ok to just borrow what you need right now, warmth or a boundary or direction, just like you would borrow a cup of sugar from a neighbor.
Next, put on your adult hat as if you are an apprentice adult and do or say what you think you should do or say. You should do at least part of what you think you should do or say.
Return the adult hat, noticing what you borrowed and what you were able to do on your own (even if it’s only 5%).
The adult hat is only borrowed, so you’re still making the choice. The longer version of this exercise can be found in my Inner Child Self-Love Reparenting Guide.
You don’t have to have trustworthy people in your history. Use someone you remember when that helps, or just imagine a good adult whose intention is to take good care of you. See if you can imagine what they would say/do in your situation, with your history, limitations, options, etc. If you can’t imagine a good adult, or just imagining a caring grown-up makes you feel more threatened, or lonelier, start smaller, with the least cruel response you can believe. Once you’ve found something good, try it, don’t keep doing the exercise.
It can be helpful to use borrowing when you’re in the adult position and not knowing what a decent adult would do, especially when the child doesn’t trust you and every response you can think of is retaliating, defending your goodness, collapsing or leaving. How would a decent adult hear that distrust? Borrow that one response. You may still feel young when you do it, it’s okay, feeling like an adult can come after you act like one.
You can choose to let the parts of you that feel younger express themselves without handing over the adult part of you to the caretaker in another person or without actually going back in age. In this way, you can access all of the positive aspects of what it can be like to feel younger such as feeling wonder, silliness, approaching things through the senses more, feeling it’s ok to be vulnerable, to let someone take care of you, to feel need, and to want to offload some decision making, while your adult part stays present.
“It is okay for a younger part of me to talk. But I understand that the adult in me is always going to be here, listening, evaluating, protecting me and stopping me if needed. I am not going to replace my adult judgement with any child state, guide, recording or person.”
This way you get the benefits of being young: curiosity, spontaneity, play, sensation, the ability to state your needs, to feel easily etc without any of the negatives of being a child, like obeying, being helpless, being scolded, the lack of good judgement etc.
What if your little one doesn’t believe you love them? It is possible to love them even if they don’t believe you love them. It is possible for trust to question your promises, remember when you failed to protect them, and take its time.
You could say something like, “Okay. I believe that you don’t believe me. I still love you. You don’t have to love me back. Tell me what feels unsafe.” Try not to turn “I still love you” into a line you say on cue, though, because then it can brush the anger off, and what it’s really saying is “so stop being angry.”
Then respond to the complaints that are sure to come. You don’t have to accept every conclusion they reach about you, but do listen for the concrete complaint without fighting the yelling and swearing around it, because even if they are coming from a place that is not completely “right,” there will likely be something true in what they are saying. If it’s something serious, answer it seriously. Do what you can to show your love for them. This might include some or all of the following: Learning to listen to them when they are angry without hitting back. Owning what was not okay. Working on changing yourself so that you are less likely to turn on them. Finding other ways to make up to them for what you did. Finding other ways to show your love for them (this might include taking care of them, such as by buying and cooking food for them, setting limits for them, taking them to the doctor when they need it, and doing what you said you would do). Just not hitting back is enough to start being the adult, even if it isn’t enough yet for them to trust you. That takes warmth, and if there isn’t any yet, borrow some.
Be aware of what you are teaching your other positions. For example, are you teaching your little one that you are going to love them no matter what? Or are you teaching them that it is their responsibility to believe your love for them, and that if they don’t, it is their fault? Is it two separate positions, one making the vow to love your little one no matter what, and the other blaming your little one for not taking in your love? Or is it one position doing both of these things? Or are you blending them? Their age might not be your chronological age. Both talk in your grown-up voice, so to your little one they’re the same. Be careful not to take the blaming as proof your love really is conditional, when it could just be another part talking.
When you’re placing your younger self on trial, instead of asking which age of you deserves the blame, ask: What was that age of you trying to get, or get away from? What did it understand back then? What options could it actually see? Could it stand to take any of them? What happened because of the choice it made? What was missing? Some ability, or help/protection from someone else? What can you learn or repair now, and how would you act differently in such situations? Even if what it did was harmful to you and others, punishing yourself now is not going to give it the capacity it needed at the time.
There is a simple and easy body technique to connect with your inner child. Just place one hand in the center of your chest which is physically connecting you to your love and then place your other hand just below that, on your solar plexus, where your child can be.
Begin to send love from your heart down to your child and just notice what comes up for you. If some comes back up, let it, and send it on down again, so it goes around like a loop. That part’s a gift from them, and they don’t owe it to you, so if nothing comes back, just keep sending yours. If you feel resistance, just meet it with love. If you feel or see something, just meet that with love as well. No warmth today? Then rest your hands there and notice what you find, no faking required. This is a conversation with your child from your heart.
The Nurturer: Some of the work you can do as the Nurturer is to enjoy your inner child. You don’t have to move their feelings, just sit back and enjoy their company. Be happy that they are there. Children need to be enjoyed! Say things to your inner child like:
It’s okay to feel the way you’re feeling.
I want you to know that I’m here for you.
You don’t need to do anything right now.
It’s okay. You’re not too much. You can be small here.
You can be angry here.
You can be sad here.
As the Protector, work with setting boundaries together. They can be simple like, “I’m going to leave this conversation because it’s not safe” or “I’m going to stop texting the person who destabilizes me.” It can be self-care boundaries like, “I’m going to eat” or “I’m going to get some sleep.” It can be trust-related boundaries like, “I’m going to keep the promise to myself” or “I’m not going to leave you to do adult things by yourself.” You can protect your inner child from yourself too, like by repairing after an internal attack: calling yourself an idiot for losing your keys again, for one. Your inner child was listening, so you go back and apologize to them.
A lot of times, inner child work doesn’t work because people are doing all the fluffy stuff but then they go and text the person who is destabilizing them, or they don’t eat, or they don’t do whatever it is they’re supposed to be doing.
If it’s hard to bring up the warm stuff, you can always do something to protect your inner child. Make sure it’s small enough that you can actually do it. If you’re not able to, figure out what’s getting in the way of you doing it. Are you scared? Tired? Do you not know how to? Is there a practical thing that’s getting in your way? Have you set yourself up to do it in a way that’s likely to be successful? Don’t make it so that doing it successfully means you have to feel good about it, or be able to check it off a list.
You can also work with your Guide. Call them whatever you want, Leader, Guru, Wise One, Sage, Inner Teacher, Director, Higher Adult, whatever.
Ask them for help with directing your life. The Guide holds standards, the way a good parent would, and asks hard things of your inner child so it can grow, at its own pace. Your parent’s harsh tone doesn’t come with the job, though, so be careful not to ask for the kind of “tough it out, you don’t have needs, you just need discipline!” kind of direction. Without the Guide, you can also slide from looking after your inner child into spoiling it: sweets and screens can pass for loving yourself, and so can getting it out of anything hard. Ask them for help in directing you to do adult things in a way that takes your needs into account: asking for the help you need, expressing your preferences, letting a safe person see you in an imperfect way, finding ways to get your need for closeness met without punishing someone for their need for space, etc. etc.
Affirmations might be helpful here, too: “We’re not just here to feel good. We’re here to become whole. We’re here to belong to life, not only to people who approve of us. We’re here to serve truth/beauty/love/God/source/nature/the universe/dharma/the Tao/the benefit of all beings,” etc. etc.
Start with whatever adult function you can connect to, but most of us need enough Nurturer and Protector first, before the Guide. Otherwise the Guide just overrules your inner child in the name of something higher (spiritual bypassing, dressed up as direction). Even if you start with protection and can’t do the warmth stuff yet, make sure the direction you’re being led in is appropriate for your inner child’s growth (i.e. not depriving them of things they need, like play or support, etc.)
Feel free to use parts language here, too, if it’s helpful. Often, we see a sensation or a distraction or an objection as something that needs to be explored, when in fact it might just be hunger, or reasonable skepticism about something, or a sentence that doesn’t fit. It’s good to notice it, though, and then to see what might be going on.
If you’re not careful, you might find yourself expecting that when you go within to meet your inner child, you’ll find your inner child.
Instead, you might feel numb, cynical, angry, hungry, like you need to look at your phone, sexually aroused, like you need to make plans, sleepy, dissociated, or you might even think that what you’re doing is stupid. Those are not failures. Often what you’re experiencing is a very charming guard. It’s what protects you when your consciously installed parental Protector isn’t functioning, the same as when you were a child. But before you decide where it’s coming from, ask it what it’s trying to stop, or what it wants. It could also be your inner child, mad that you took so long to come back, or your inherited parent script, or something from earlier today, or a bit of each.
(To the guard, in the same Nurturer voice you meant for your inner child: “I see you. I’m not going to force my way past you. What’s going on?” Then wait and listen patiently. If nothing comes, that’s fine for now. At some point you can ask, “What are you afraid would happen if you stopped protecting me by…..?”)
If necessary take time and listen. It can be difficult to connect with your inner child if your inner child didn’t have the opportunity to develop. This happens often when you grow up in a situation where you don’t have a private self, for example when a controlling family, a rigid religion or an enmeshed community takes over very early in your life. Or you are pushed to achieve very early in life. The result is that you don’t know what you feel, what you want, what you believe, what you like and dislike until you have heard someone else’s opinion about it. If you are in that situation, it can be difficult to follow the advice to ‘love yourself’. You don’t even know who ‘yourself’ is! So you can do reparenting and finding yourself in parallel. For others, it is very easy to work with the inner child, they can feel it easily.
You are in the first camp if:
You don’t know what you want, until you have heard what someone else wants.
Your opinion is very different when you are with different people
You agree with people in the moment but when you are by yourself you realize that you don’t agree with them
You take responsibility for the emotions of others, at the expense of yourself
When you try to love yourself, it feels more like a show
When you try to find out how your inner child feels, you feel that you are guessing instead of feeling
You can rebel, but you can’t choose yet
One way of explaining this is that in your childhood you didn’t spend enough attention in finding out what you like and what you want to try out and who you are when nobody is grading you. You were too busy avoiding pain, reading what was dangerous and what you had to do to stay in a good bond, etc.

As you become more your own person, you learn to tell which of those apply. You want to let your quieter preferences bubble up to the surface so you can be sure you’re not just echoing your social group.
What is the difference between a human being and a human doing? If you don’t feel good enough as a human being, you will try to become good enough as a “human doing” by, for example, being beautiful, doing something well, being smart, having a certain status, being spiritual, etc. Those can all be real gifts, although they still become a kind of bargain for belonging when failing in these areas feels like losing what it means to have your own inherent value.
So in order to find yourself, you can ask yourself:
What do I like when nobody is looking?
What do I believe when I don’t check with other people?
What do I want that is neither in rebellion nor in compliance with others?
Where am I buying my sense of belonging at the expense of betraying myself?
What can I try on that I don’t need to be good at?
With whom can I be myself?
What do I feel in my body and what do I make out of it?
Give your inner child the opportunity to do something that has no value for its resume and that it doesn’t need to be good at. For example painting, dancing, gardening, learning a language, playing a sport, doing volunteer work, playing a musical instrument, etc. Because often your inherited parent script tells your inner child that it is supposed to be good at something as soon as it starts doing it, which is humiliating. The more consciously sculpted adult in you can answer, “We’re finding out whether we enjoy this, not proving our worth.” So try things out long enough until the humiliation is gone.
When you are a child you feel that you need to belong to the family in order to survive. This is why people do things for their family, religion, romantic partner, political tribe, spiritual group, institution, online community etc., that they wouldn’t otherwise do. Part of adulting is working out where you are selling yourself in order to belong and choosing your own ground, and finding out you can disappoint someone and not disappear. A large part of your subconscious mind is made out of other people. That is why you are reading a self hypnosis guide!
Where am I betraying myself in order to belong?
What does it feel like to belong without betraying myself?
Where do I think I am following my own guidance, but I am in fact following my belonging program?
Where do I think I am doing things out of love, but I am actually doing it out of fear of not belonging?
Where do I think I am listening to my conscience, but I am actually listening to my conditioning?
Where do I think I am doing something out of devotion, but I am actually doing it out of compliance?
Where do I think I am free, but I am actually rebelling?
And then look what your body tells you. It is not always correct, but it is a good place to start.
One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is that sudden “waking up” to all the ways your attention is being shaped in your day-to-day life. There are actually multiple patents on using screens to send subliminal messages, but even without that kind of potentially illegal tech, the screen is one connection to the omnipotent Algorithm. Which shows us ads and guides our preferences. Then we wonder why we vote for this or that politician. But there are also the older, more mundane influences: erotic imprinting (as if breast implants are actually sexy), religious fear, which tags along with shame, charismatic authority and pressure to belong. And all of that drilled repeatedly into us, because one exposure won’t do the trick. Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.
Manipulation often comes with any of the following: urgency, you are special, FOMO (fear of missing out), not being included, sexual charge, shame, confused, someone will rescue you, destiny, you should obey, secret knowledge, an excessive sense of certainty about something way too quickly, and a sense that one good question will break the spell.
First of all, if you sense you are being hypnotically influenced, stop. Don’t obey immediately, but don’t rebel automatically, just realize that you are being influenced.
Secondly, some of the ways that hypnotic language is used to manipulate are where you have consented to something without realizing it, where you are given only one choice, or where something not yet agreed upon is embedded in a sentence. For example;
You will soon realize that I am right …. Or you may, in time, decide to admit that …. Or the only reason you do not agree is …. Or part of you already knows …. Or your higher self wants …. Or everyone who is awake knows …. Or the reason you do not believe that is true is because your ego does not want you to …
If you are unsure, you may like to ask yourself the following questions;
What am I being asked to agree to? What choice am I being given? What is being assumed that I may not agree with? Who benefits if I comply? What is the emotionally charged part of what is being said? What is not being said? If I say no, what will the consequences be? (Will I be punished, shamed, laughed at, not be included, be told I am not ‘awake’ etc?)

Be aware that even when using permissive language, you can still take away the subject’s choice. Be aware of;
Indirect suggestions can by-pass the subject’s skeptical guard. They do this by not directly telling the subject what to do. This does not mean that indirect suggestions are not specific. It simply means that they are worded in a vague, conversational, suggestive manner.
1) Utilizing induction techniques while seemingly explaining something (even something like “anti hypnosis” can use the same mechanics of induction).
2) In any way making it so that whatever the subject says shows that a suggestion has worked, when this may not be the case (this includes answering yes, no, noticing something, not noticing something, trying not to do something, not answering, etc etc etc)
3) Including phrases such as whether or not you notice etc etc, so either way counts as success
4) Including any concepts that may make a subject think they must obey, or take on a role, or that it is good/safe to please the guide or belong to someone etc etc.
5) Fractionating a subject without telling them that you are going to take them in and out of absorption a few times.
6) Giving a subject cues (words, gestures, blinks, sounds, listening a certain number of times etc) that you intend to use to make them do something at a later date, without informing them exactly what it is that they will be doing.
7) Including suggestions for amnesia, or making a subject think that something (dream, amnesia, imagery, body experiences etc) has happened when this may not necessarily be the case.
8) Not taking a subject out at the end of a recording, or leaving them with a role to play, with their judgement down, with their physical abilities down, with their minds blank, or in any other way different for an indefinite length of time.
In order for a subject to be making a REAL choice whilst in a hypnosis, there MUST be at least one way for a subject NOT to carry on with the hypnosis if they wish. This could be by making the hypnosis lighter, using a different method of hypnosis, being in full awareness whilst in a hypnosis, or being able to pause or stop the hypnosis. Just so you know, if you say no, you are quite entitled to mean NO, even if someone with a nice voice is asking you to do something! Also, just because you don’t say anything, or don’t know what to say, DOES NOT mean yes!

Getting yourself ready to do something. Part of that is gathering your attention up. Part of that might be deepening. If you have gone somewhere, make sure to go back the same way you went there. Etcetera.
Here is a generic bring-back that you can use: “When I come out of this session, I will only bring with me that which is useful to me in my everyday life right now. Anything else I will bring with me at a later date, when I am better able to integrate it. When I come out of this session, I will be coming back to the room I am in now, and to the day in which I am participating in this session now. All the instructions to carry me deeper into this session or keep me in this state are now finished. The only intention I will take with me into my everyday life, and the only cue I will use to take me into this state at a later date, will be the ones I consciously choose, and neither of them will keep me in this state. When I come out of this session I will be me, in my body and with my adult judgment.”
Then do a count up: On 1 start to feel your body again and what it’s resting on and feel your weight (of your choice). On 2 start to feel your breathing return to normal. On 3 start to hear the room around you and name where you are. On 4 start to wiggle your fingers and toes, move your shoulders and your eyes. On 5 open your eyes, back in the here and now, feeling normal and clear and the session is now over.
When you come out make sure you can name what day (or date) it is, look to your left and right, look at something near to you and something further away. Move around a bit. Don’t get up until you feel like you can do so without falling over. Make sure that you are oriented and alert (counting does this, but not always). Take mental note of only what actually came up for you and any actions you need to take regarding it. Then go on and do something normal.
If your recording cuts out for some reason, you can say to yourself, “The recording has stopped and the session is over,” and then do the above on your own. Once your eyes are open, press your feet or hands into a surface as well.
Note: If you are going to sleep to a recording then it is fine to go to sleep or just remain resting quietly at the end of it. However, if you are coming out of a recording then you should not leave yourself in an altered state. Note: If you have a tendency to daydream, dissociate or fall asleep, it is better to do this exercise sitting up and save lying down for when you want to go to sleep, get a very deep rest or incubate dreams. If you are sitting, keep your spine straight but not rigid like a soldier. Relax your jaw and stay somewhat connected to the room you are in.
“I am not leaving life; I am listening more deeply to life.
I invoke my Higher Self, universal heart-mind, wise subconscious mind, intelligence in my body, inner child(ren), inner adult(s), guard(s) and all that is of truth and love to help me know what I need to know, only in a form and at a time that will be useful, kind, stabilizing and real for me.”
Ask your conscious mind to listen.
This does not mean you have to stop thinking to listen. Just notice your thoughts, body sensations, pictures, doubts, emotions, etc. Don’t fight what comes up, but don’t go with it either. Just notice what stands out on its own as you hold the idea of what you are doing in the back of your mind.
Internally say, “Tell me what I need to know or ask me what you need to know and I’ll sit in silence for 5 minutes and listen.”
You may hear a phrase, feel a body sensation, notice a memory, see a color, be contacted by a child or guard, feel pain, warmth, complete silence, know that you need to do something, be grateful for something, feel you need to stop the listening or any number of things.
Listen to everything and believe nothing automatically.
Read through these sections, and then try doing the inner meeting without looking at the screen.
Respond to each thing that comes up with an accurate notice and a small reasonable invitation (or action or taking more time etc). The thing might be a sensation, image, gesture, feeling, words, or anything. The notice and invitation don’t need to cover all those forms, just notice and invite what happens.
An example notice might be, “I notice my chest tightening when I imagine asking for help”. Don’t add interpretation like “this must be the abandoned child part of me, or a protective mechanism” - just notice what you notice. An example invitation might be, “And as I notice that, I can take some time before deciding what it means, and notice if I want to say anything, or change it, or just stay like that”.
Then just listen. You don’t need fancy language - often it will be better to just ask what happens next, or whatever. If you notice a feeling developing, it might be best not to say anything while it’s developing (if you can help it) but some days you need to talk to understand, so just do that.
You can be pretty straightforward when that’s the help you chose - “Let the explanation wait a moment. What do I feel as I say that?” can be a perfectly valid thing to say to yourself, and help you focus. As long as you’re still present, and able to change if you want to, and happy to carry on, a sad feeling or tension or whatever doesn’t require an exit.
It’s worth trying to separate the notice, the meaning, and your thoughts on the meaning, but in practice it will often be pretty fuzzy. When you can, it can be helpful to separate it out like that though - “I noticed... this seemed to mean... here’s why that might be true / false” or something like that.
Is this a notice or meaning? “My stomach went tight” is a notice, “He’s a complete bastard” is a meaning, even if you didn’t think it in words. You can then go on to find out what he did, notice what it was that gave you the idea, and consider if there might be other explanations. It’s also ok to put a meaning into words now, to look at it, even if it came to you without words. Nonverbal thoughts and early thoughts aren’t necessarily any deeper, truer, or more reliable than other thoughts. Feelings are good to pay attention to, but it’s still good to consider what they mean.
Your shoulders tightening, or ‘hmm, that feels kind of wrong’, is a signal to investigate further, but ‘No! That is Not Right!’ is a signal to stop what you’re doing and change it. If you don’t feel like it fits, don’t keep doing it. Just change it. You don’t need any other reason.
“I notice the tightness, and I can just leave it like that. I wonder if that fits, or if I’d rather do something different?”
Sometimes the invitation just isn’t right - sometimes it’s something you hadn’t thought of. Either way, it isn’t automatically a guard, and silence doesn’t mean a hidden process is working.

Try and be specific in your description, and be willing to alter it if you find out that it was incorrect. Just because someone is disagreeing with you or trying to set boundaries around you does not mean they are in their emotionally immature parts. You don’t need to subject yourself to something that may be dangerous before protecting yourself.
On the other hand, you may find that you feel guilty. Having feelings of guilt does not mean that you have done something wrong or that you have been manipulated. Have you done something that was wrong or that caused harm? If so, what can you do to fix it? On the other hand, did you give in to someone else just to keep them from being disappointed in you? What do you want to do or achieve the next time you interact with this person? Do you need them to understand what you are feeling/thinking? Do you just need to communicate information to them? This is called pendulation, and approaching in smaller amounts is titration. Do as much or as little as you feel you can.
“Ok, I think that is enough for now.”

You do not need to act out the urge, shake, release, etc. If you do move and you feel that you are causing yourself pain or other symptoms that you are concerned about, stop moving.
If any younger parts come up, offer them the opportunity to spend time with you, or some space if they would rather. If one of them says “don’t come closer”, stay at the distance they choose. You don’t have to consider them literally younger, nor do you have to ask them why they are there or what happened to them. If you are already able to do a certain step, you don’t have to do it again.
Try some different ideas as to what might be helpful for this inner part to feel better (being welcomed by you, visualizing someone else, giving them the sort of words they would like to hear, you placing yourself in a different body position, you moving further away etc). Only try one idea at a time to see if it works.
It is possible that when you try and give the part what it wants, you might feel very upset. It may be that it never got what it needed at the time and now that you are giving it what it wants, it is processing the upset of not getting what it wanted before. If this happens, allow yourself to respond for as long as you want to do so, and for as long as you can stay there (ie remain in the process). If you feel that the voice, distance, touch, image etc is too much, then change it to something that is less. Don’t think that you can’t take the love.
Allow yourself to see where a metaphor takes you. Ask questions like ‘if the problem had an image or story, what would it be?’ or ‘what would need to happen to make things right?’ If it feels like you need to do something to give yourself the resource that you feel you need (or to put a boundary in place, or to move away or to take some other action) then try doing that for as far as it takes to be of use to you. Remember that whatever you find out is likely to be metaphorical. It may be a good hypothesis for what you need to do but it is not a proven fact.
Alternatively, you may want to use the session to develop a capacity that you want to develop (ie love, play, courage, curiosity etc). You can also use it to rehearse something that you have decided to do.
Don’t feel that you have to end the session with a great revelation! When you have done as much as you want to do, it is a good idea to find out if there is anything that you need to do to make sure that you can leave things where they are for the time being. This might include thanking parts for their help, or making sure that you do something in real life (eat a good meal, put a boundary in place, get some rest, repair a relationship, keep a promise etc). Whatever it is, tell your little one, “That’s enough for today. We’re going back to the life we’re building.”
When you have finished, even if you stopped part way through, use the ‘Come all the way back’ procedure to bring yourself back. When you are back, it is a good idea to write a few lines in a notebook about what you have done. Just jot down the essentials (what was there before you started, what you have done to change things, what you are unsure about, any phrases that were said, any body signals, any information that the inner child said that it needed, anything that a guard wanted you to know, any boundaries that you put in place, any repairs that you did, anything that you learnt about what it is a mistake to try and force etc). You don’t need to write down the whole cast of characters, just what you actually noticed.
Note: throughout the exercise, allow your analytical part to make comments and/or tell you that it doesn’t like what you are doing. Just tell it that you will check things out when you come back and make any commitments etc when you are back. If it says no to going deeper, or tells you to stop doing the exercise, I’d stop there and not push past that no, even when it sounds like a prediction. You can stop whenever you want to. Remember that the images that you see can be meaningful without being actual memories of things that happened and just because you see an image, or feel a body release, that doesn’t mean that you are right about what is going on!
Notice there is no need to learn a second script! The process is the same. You are simply practicing for fifteen minutes or so. That is long enough to induce yourself (it only takes a few minutes), practice and let it unfold at its own pace, and come out again (that takes a few minutes too). Five minutes is plenty to see what happens when you simply sit in silence, listening, and you can interrupt yourself at any time to change direction if that feels better.
You can also try other ways of inducing yourself such as becoming aware of 3 things you can see, 3 things you can hear, 3 things you can feel in your body; then 2 of each, 1 of each. Then count from 5 to 1 and begin to listen. Choose one way to induce yourself, you don’t need to try all of them! (In fact, it might be counter-productive!)
Once you have practiced listening a few times with the recordings, you may want to shorten them to speed up your induction, or even practice without playing them back at all. On the other hand, if you like using the recordings, there is no reason to stop! (NB. You may wish to use the re-entry cue to help you re-enter your process, this will also shorten your induction if you already know what to do.)
As you come out of the process ask yourself what needed warmth, what needed to be protected, what you need to do differently to be more in accord with truth and love and life. Is there something you want to explore more fully or a capacity you want to build? And most importantly, what can you carry with you as you move forward from this? If you identified something you needed to do differently, make a plan with yourself to do that thing. The more specific you can be, the more likely you are to change: “If _________ (fill in the cue for the old pattern), then I will do ________ (fill in one small action that will begin to change the pattern).” Then check back later and see how you are doing – sleeping, relating, functioning, etc., not only how impressive the session felt.
It’s good to give this more time once or twice a week, when that’s useful. It doesn’t have to be very intense but it is good to start from Higher Self or at least a neutral witnessing place and follow what appears. It’s also good to bring in some adult function to make sure nothing is being bypassed and so that at the end of the exercise, when the experience is over, there is the possibility of coming out completely and doing whatever normal thing needs doing.
If possible, it’s good to do the normal thing immediately after the exercise, so that the subconscious sees that the adult heard and acted. Otherwise, the dishes won’t get done.
NOTE: If it is medically unsafe or you are in a place of panic, sleep deprivation, nausea, deep destabilization, mania, psychosis-like symptoms, feeling overwhelmed by chemicals etc. then first focus on stabilizing and then look for what your subconscious needs you to know! If it takes you destabilizing to know what your subconscious knows, it is not meant for you to know directly at this time! Focus on asking for capacity over content!
Sometimes, it feels like your subconscious knows something that your conscious self is not prepared to know. It may be something related to your sexuality, grief, trauma, family issues, betrayal, shame, vocation, a relationship, illness fears, spirituality, addiction, identity, moral issues etc.
What you DON’T want to do is bully your subconscious into telling you what it knows by saying things to yourself like:
“What is it you won’t tell me? What are you hiding? Tell me NOW! I am telling you to tell me!”
This can lead to flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation etc. and can make your day SUCK! When you are flooded, it is much harder to access your adult capacities so focus on being able to regulate and getting support! Just ask for what you need to know in a way that you CAN tolerate:

Instead, say to yourself something like this:
“Dear Wise Subconscious Mind, if there is something you know that my conscious self is not ready to know, please don’t break it open violently! Do what you can to make me able to know it in a way that is safe! Prepare me BEFORE you break it open! Ground me BEFORE you show me the memory! Support me BEFORE you make it intense! Give me one next action!” etc.
REMEMBER: Not everything in hypnotic imagery is literal, especially if it relates to trauma and memory. The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc. So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!

Comfort your little one before you answer any of it. Your answers can be firm or funny, as long as they aren’t mean. Then work on finding some ordinary evidence to build a more believable ‘grown up’ voice of your own.
If the fake feeling is telling you that you don’t have the grown up ability to do this yet, then don’t try and convince yourself by using an inner voice. As long as you can still observe yourself well enough to do this, try and borrow what you need from someone who you can imagine is good enough to lend it to you. Try out something which rings true to you, whether it is a sentence, an action etc, and see how you get on.
There may not be an answer. There may not be an answer that will help you. You may need to try asking a different question or you may just need to rest or finish your inner work for the day.
